names.value: Digital Text and Data Analysis TEN
Digital Text and Data Analysis TEN

descriptions.text:
This course introduces students of the humanities to the fundamentals of digital text analysis. It explores how computational methods can be used to study language, literature, and cultural texts in new and systematic ways. Students will learn key approaches from corpus linguistics, digital discourse analysis, and related fields, while gaining practical experience with tools and techniques for analyzing textual data.

Designed for beginners, the course requires no prior programming experience. Through a combination of conceptual discussions and hands-on exercises, students will learn how to collect, prepare, and analyze textual corpora, and how to interpret the results critically within a humanities framework.

By the end of the course, students will understand both the possibilities and limitations of digital methods for studying texts and discourse, and will be able to apply basic analytical techniques to their own research interests.
All reading materials will be announced via Brightspace.

### Assessment

* Mid-term exam: Written examination with closed questions
* Final exam: Written examination with short open questions

### Weighing

* Mid-term exam: (50 percent of grade)
* Final exam: (50 percent of grade)

The final mark for the course is established by determining the weighted average. In order to pass the course, students must have a grade of at least 5.5 for both mid-term exam and the final exam.

General information about registering for courses and exams can be found [here](https://www.student.universiteitleiden.nl/en/your-study-programme/courses-and-exams/enrolment/humanities/dutch-studies-ba?cf=humanities&cd=dutch-studies-ba#tab-1).

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

* Understand the key concepts and approaches in digital text analysis, corpus linguistics, and digital discourse analysis
* Explain how computational methods can support research in the humanities
* Apply basic text analysis techniques such as word frequency analysis, concordances, collocations, and keyword analysis
* Use beginner-friendly digital tools to explore and analyze textual data
* Interpret quantitative results in relation to qualitative, critical perspectives
* Reflect on methodological choices, limitations, and ethical considerations in digital humanities research
This course is open to all students of the Faculty of Humanities.

* For substantive questions; contact the lecturer listed in the right information bar.* For questions about enrolment; admission; etc.; contact the Education Administration Office: [Reuvensplaats](https://www.organisatiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/faculteiten-en-instituten/geesteswetenschappen/faculteitsbureau/onderwijs--en-studentzaken/onderwijsondersteuning/onderwijsadministratie-reuvensplaats).

Attendance and active participation are obligatory. Students are required to prepare for and attend all sessions. The lecturer needs to be informed without delay of any classes missed for a good reason (i.e. due to unforeseen circumstances such as illness; family issues; problems with residence permits). The maximum of such absences during a semester is two. Being absent without notification and/or more than two times can result in exclusion from the exams and a failing grade for the course.

* Dispensation from the attendance policy for extenuating circumstances can only be granted by the[ ](https://www.student.universiteitleiden.nl/studie-en-studeren/studie/onderwijsinformatie/examencommissie/geesteswetenschappen/koreastudies-ba?cf=geesteswetenschappen&cd=koreastudies-ba#tab-2)Board of Examiners examencommissietw@hum.leidenuniv.nl after consultation with the coordinator of studies stuco-digitalhumanities@hum.leidenuniv.nl.

### Resit

A resit will be offered for both the mid-term and the final exam, each in the same format as the original.

### Inspection and feedback

How and when an exam review will take place will be disclosed together with the publication of the exam results at the latest. If a student requests a review within 30 days after publication of the exam results, an exam review will have to be organized.

descriptions.value: Acquiring knowledge by systematically and methodically inquiring into a situation or concept, making use of methods appropriate to the academic field or discipline.
Kennis verwerven door het systematisch en methodisch bevragen van een situatie of concept waarbij gebruik gemaakt wordt van methoden die passen bij het vakgebied of de discipline.
Analysing situations or information and deciding what is of major and lesser importance. Seeing interrelationships and getting to the core of the matter.
Ontleden van situaties of een hoeveelheid informatie in hoofd- en bijzaken. Zien van onderlinge verbanden en doordringen tot de kern.
Formulating new concepts, conceptual frameworks or models based on complex information and issues.
Formuleren van nieuwe concepten, denkkaders of modellen op basis van complexe informatie en vraagstukken.
Achieving a result by effectively and systematically utilising and overseeing activities, time and resources.
Een resultaat bereiken door het effectief en planmatig inzetten en overzien van activiteiten, tijd en middelen.
Using digital technology, methods, sources or databases to achieve results.
Gebruiken van digitale technologie, methoden, bronnen of databases om resultaten te behalen.
Contributing to a joint result with other people or groups, even when this is not in your own personal interest.
Bijdragen aan een gezamenlijk resultaat met andere personen of groepen, ook wanneer dit niet van direct persoonlijk belang is.
Setting out ideas and information clearly in writing, taking account of the relevant target group and in such a way that the message is received and understood.
Ideeën en informatie helder op schrift stellen, rekening houdend met de doelgroep, en zodanig dat de boodschap overkomt en wordt begrepen.

Critically evaluating own and others’ behaviour, viewpoints or methods, and being open to evaluation by others. Being able to learn from these evaluations by changing own behaviour, viewpoints or methods.

Het kritisch evalueren van (eigen) gedrag, standpunten of methoden en open staan voor evaluatie door anderen. Het vermogen om te leren van deze evaluaties door wijziging van het eigen gedrag, standpunten of methoden.
Self-directing own process of absorbing and applying new knowledge and information.
Zelf sturing geven aan het eigen proces van nieuwe kennis en informatie opnemen en toepassen.
